solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mixed metaphors in Moliere play

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of metaphors and in are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A drama critic complains of muddled imagery in a French comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like the start of the phrase 'mixed metaphors', but it is the anagram signal working on METAPHORS plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Misanthrope is a famous comedy by the French playwright Moliere.

clue.text: I'm a Muslim leader? Yes

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether he is an Islamic leader and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the M from Muslim. The whole clue is also a self-description by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and is a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Not in favour of social worker being put over one

indicators.note: in a down entry, being put over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: the ant is a social insect, and a worker ant is a classic crossword social worker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An opponent of a care worker being promoted above someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a council care worker, but it is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to oppose it, not favour it.

clue.text: Essay I can write up in college

indicators.note: in tells us those pieces go inside the first

parts.note: an essay is an attempt or try
the letter I as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means written from the bottom, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A student writing an essay at university.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'write up' means reading upwards, so the can is turned before it joins I inside the essay word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is the name of colleges at Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin.

clue.text: Paradoxical criterion of stability

parts.note: the paradox is that the word means something firmly fixed yet also means to sway back and forth

explanation.definitionFit: A rock is a byword for stability, yet to rock is to sway unsteadily.

clue.text: Go on — take legal action

definitions.meaning: to bring a lawsuit against someone

explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to carry on, and to proceed against someone is to sue them.

clue.text: Drivers making a commotion amid applause

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cheers are applause
a riot is a commotion

explanation.surface: Racing drivers stir up trouble among a clapping crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists or golf clubs, but these drove horse-drawn chariots.
explanation.definitionFit: Charioteers were the drivers of horse-drawn chariots in ancient races and battles.

clue.text: Settlement of rent, once due, needs to be met

indicators.note: settlement suggests sorting things out, so the letters of rent once due are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying off back rent is a demand that must be satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'met' looks like 'satisfied', as a demand is met, but it means came across.
explanation.definitionFit: To have met someone is to have come across them.

clue.text: Eastern country lacking a prominent feature

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: China is a country in the East
the letter A as written

explanation.surface: An Asian nation is said to have nothing that stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaw's front point is a prominent facial feature, especially a jutting one.

clue.text: Two members of the crew sailed round New Zealand

parts.note: a captain is one member of a ship's crew
a cook is another member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A pair of sailors circumnavigated New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the man: the explorer James Cook charted New Zealand's coast on his first voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain James Cook, the eighteenth-century navigator, circumnavigated and mapped New Zealand.

clue.text: Vivacity seen in Brazilian capital and port

indicators.note: a capital letter here is the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, Rio for short

explanation.surface: Liveliness is spotted in Brazil's capital city and harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazilian capital' suggests Brasilia, but 'capital' is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is an Italian-derived word for spirited liveliness or verve.

clue.text: Pleasant setting for the national team?

definitions.meaning: a side chosen to represent a nation

explanation.definitionFit: Countryside is rural land; split, it reads as a country's side or team.

clue.text: Magazines laid so price may be seen

indicators.note: may be seen hints that the right word can be spotted when the letters of laid so price are rearranged

explanation.surface: Magazines are displayed so their cost is visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodicals are magazines or journals published at regular intervals.

clue.text: Cut and run

definitions.meaning: a surgeon cuts a patient open during surgery
to run a machine or business is to work it

explanation.definitionFit: To operate is both to perform surgery and to work or manage something.

clue.text: Soldier seen in the overturned boat

indicators.note: overturned in a down entry means the whole is read from the bottom up
seen in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is spotted in a capsized boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boat' is fair because a rowing eight is named for its crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a racing rowing boat crewed by eight oarsmen.

clue.text: Decoration of stone sculpture

indicators.note: sculpture is the shaping of material, so the letters of of stone are reshaped

explanation.surface: An ornament carved out of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a decorative chain of flowers or ribbons hung in a curve.

clue.text: Circus performers? Maybe true or false

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word false could become another arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about circus acts, which may or may not be real.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: flea circuses are a famous, often faked, sideshow, hence 'true or false'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea circuses claimed to show trained fleas pulling tiny carts and performing tricks.

clue.text: Give in or give out

definitions.meaning: to produce, as a crop or investment produces a return

explanation.definitionFit: Yielding is surrendering, and a yield is also the output a field or investment produces.

clue.text: Article about Kipling poem of unaffected simplicity

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A piece discussing one of Kipling's verses praises its artless style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the article; 'If—' is Kipling's best-known poem, a staple of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif is a variant of naive, describing someone or something artless and unaffected.

clue.text: A venerable name in England's illustrious past

definitions.text: A venerable name in England's illustrious past

parts.words: A venerable name in England's illustrious past
parts.note: the word venerable hints at the honorific title given to an early English monk and historian

explanation.surface: A revered figure from English history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an eighth-century Northumbrian monk who wrote an ecclesiastical history of the English.

clue.text: He may be found in a wrongful act

definitions.text: He may be found in a wrongful act

indicators.note: may be found in tells us one piece sits inside another
wrongful means wrongly ordered, so the letters of act are rearranged

parts.note: the word he as written

explanation.surface: A man could be caught committing an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongful' rearranges ACT into CAT. The whole clue also describes the answer: someone caught in a dishonest act.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or fraud is someone who acts dishonestly, the very wrongdoer described.

clue.text: Get rid of players on strike

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
workers on strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: Sack the actors who have walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast out is to expel or banish, getting rid of someone.

clue.text: The French are after refreshing quiet drink

indicators.note: are after places the following piece behind the first
refreshing suggests making anew, so the letters of quiet are reworked

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: French people seek a calming, refreshing drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French are' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it gives only the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave.

clue.text: Holiday camp worker is an old soldier

definitions.meaning: an entertainer and helper at a Butlin's holiday camp in Britain, named for their red jackets
a British soldier of former times, who wore a scarlet tunic

explanation.definitionFit: Butlin's staff wear red jackets, and historic British infantry wore red coats.

clue.text: No longer bound to deliver

explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to release them, leaving them no longer tied up.

clue.text: Blow on the foot for warmth

definitions.meaning: a garment worn over the foot to keep it warm

explanation.definitionFit: A sock is slang for a punch, and also a knitted foot covering.

clue.text: Duck and swan up in the air

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the zero-shaped letter O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Water birds flying overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the air' reads as birds in flight but means undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: A question still open is undecided, which is what up in the air means.

clue.text: A light head-band

parts.note: a band of light round the head, as painted on saints, rather than a hair accessory

explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light shown around the head of a holy figure.

clue.text: Near average

definitions.meaning: near is old slang for stingy
the arithmetic average of a set

explanation.definitionFit: Mean can be stingy, as near is, and the arithmetic average of a set.

clue.text: Agreed about spiteful woman being involved

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: complied means agreed or went along with
cat is a slang word for a spiteful woman

explanation.surface: Someone consented to dealings with a malicious woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiteful woman' for CAT is an old, unflattering crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involved has many intricate parts, which is to say it is complex.

clue.text: Blockhead student in a spot

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: a dot is a spot
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A dim pupil finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside DOT. 'In a spot' reads as 'in trouble' but just gives DOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a stupid, slow-witted person.

clue.text: Buy drinks and loaf

definitions.meaning: to ... is to pay for drinks for the group in a pub

explanation.definitionFit: Standing a round is British pub idiom for treating everyone; standing around is idling.
